title: Boolean Functions Under Non-Uniform Inputs and Fixed-Degree Approximation
summary: The paper relies on uniform-input properties and fixed-degree truncation, leaving non-uniform behavior and the best fixed-degree approximation unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For Boolean functions, characterize their behavior under non-uniform input distributions and determine the best approximation achievable at each fixed degree; this approximation is needed to analyze higher-order correlation attacks.

scope.domain: Structural analysis of Boolean functions in symmetric cryptography, with distributional and approximation questions relevant to higher-order correlation attacks.
parameters: input distribution: the distribution under which Boolean-function behavior is analyzed
degree: the fixed degree used for the approximation
scope.unresolved_remainder: Characterize Boolean functions under non-uniform input distributions and determine the best approximation achievable at each fixed degree for higher-order correlation-attack analysis.

citations.label: Towards Stream Ciphers for Efficient FHE with Low-Noise Ciphertexts

progress.summary: The paper presents these as interesting problems raised by its analyses of Boolean functions. It specifically identifies non-uniform input distributions and best fixed-degree approximations, with the latter needed for higher-order correlation attacks.
citation_labels: Pierrick Méaux et al., Towards Stream Ciphers for Efficient FHE with Low-Noise Ciphertexts
